PullRequest.Title: chat: Correlate code-block copy and insert telemetry
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Make chat code-block copy/insert events attributable to the request and chat that produced the code, and avoid counting known failed operations as acceptance. This provides the core correlation needed to measure code-block actions in Agent Host chats; the shared action paths also cover local chat.

Previously, these events omitted the originating request and chat-session IDs, and an insertion could be reported even when no editor was available or the edit was not applied. The four code-block actions now populate `sourceRequestId` and canonical `chatSessionId`, using the same session identity as chat request telemetry.

Toolbar and whole-block keyboard copies report after the clipboard write resolves. Insertions report only when the bulk edit is applied, a notebook cell is created, or the new-file editor opens. Native selected-copy handling still falls through synchronously to the editor; its telemetry observes the copy gesture rather than certifying clipboard completion.

## Implementation notes

- Add the optional session field and its telemetry classification, and mark the accepted-event AH boolean as a measurement.
- Add regression coverage for local, Copilot, Claude, Codex, and remote AH correlation, failed/cancelled operations, notebook insertion, and native-copy fallback.
- This is the VS Code emitter portion only. Downstream scorecard mapping and denominator definitions require separate changes; live ingestion and end-to-end scorecard joins have not been verified.

Scenarios.Scenario: Copy a chat code block from the toolbar or with the whole-block keyboard command
Scenarios.CriticalPath: One clipboard write must complete before the newly delayed telemetry/reporting runs; the clipboard operation itself was already the user-visible copy boundary before the PR. Awaiting it extends the command promise but does not add work to clipboard completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write the code-block text to the native clipboard; browser builds use navigator.clipboard instead.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one clipboard write per explicit copy gesture, with no collection fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same single clipboard write was started per gesture without awaiting its promise.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The write is the copy operation's critical path. The diff waits for the existing operation before reporting telemetry but does not increase clipboard latency or call count.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Notify the owning chat extension of the copy action when an agent ID is present.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one extension-host notification per successful copy, unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same notification was emitted immediately after starting the clipboard write.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: For full-block copies it is now enqueued after clipboard completion rather than immediately; it is not required for the clipboard result and is not awaited.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Queue the existing codeAccepted telemetry event with two additional scalar correlation fields.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One event per successful user copy, unchanged; payload grows by request/session identifier strings only.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same event was queued with no chatSessionId and an undefined sourceRequestId.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous event preparation occurs after clipboard completion but network delivery is not awaited.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One user gesture and one code-block string; clipboard bytes scale with code length exactly as before, while added telemetry bytes scale with bounded identifier lengths.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One clipboard operation per gesture. The PR serializes reporting after that operation rather than launching additional concurrent work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache participates. Repeated gestures intentionally perform separate clipboard writes and telemetry events; there is no miss/retry amplification.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the action handlers, clipboard implementations, MultiCommand dispatch, and synchronous telemetry/event paths.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Clipboard IPC duration varies by platform, but no new call or repeated work is introduced; only command-promise/report ordering changes.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the diff preserves boundary cardinality and resource volume, and the added correlation serialization is constant per explicit gesture.

Scenarios.Scenario: Copy a selected range from the embedded code-block editor
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The changed implementation reports the action and then returns false so the existing native editor copy implementation performs the clipboard operation synchronously.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fall through to the native/editor copy implementation, which may write to the clipboard.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One native copy per keyboard gesture, unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Telemetry/reporting also ran before falling through to the same native copy implementation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Clipboard handling remains on the copy gesture's critical path; the diff does not move or duplicate it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Notify the chat extension of the copy gesture.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one notification per gesture, unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous enqueue before native copy, unchanged in placement.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Selected text length and one gesture; text extraction and telemetry delta computation already scaled with the selected text before this PR.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous gesture path; no changed parallel fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache or coalescing is used or needed for distinct copy gestures.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the changed branch and MultiCommand fallback implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Selection sizes vary, but the diff only adds constant-size identifiers and a closure.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: no expensive work was added or moved onto a hotter path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Insert a code block into the active text editor or notebook
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Text insertion waits for the existing bulk edit; notebook insertion creates one cell synchronously. The PR only checks the existing result before emitting acceptance telemetry.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Apply one ResourceTextEdit through the bulk edit service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One bulk edit containing one text edit per insertion gesture, unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same bulk edit was awaited, after which telemetry was emitted regardless of its result.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for insertion and already awaited before the PR; inspecting isApplied adds no boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Notify the chat extension of a successful insertion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one notification per successful insertion; failed insertions now emit none.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One notification was emitted after every attempted operation, including unsuccessful attempts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Occurs after the edit and is not awaited across the extension-host boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Queue codeAccepted telemetry with correlation identifiers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one event per successful insertion; the PR reduces events for failures.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One event was queued after an attempted insertion, without correlation identifiers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous event preparation after insertion; delivery is not awaited.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One code block and one target per explicit gesture. Reindent/edit construction scales with code size as before; no per-cell or per-session loop was introduced.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One bulk edit or cell insertion per gesture, serialized as before.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache participates; no repeated misses or retained keys.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from InsertCodeBlockOperation and its action caller.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Bulk-edit cost depends on code size and editor state, but the diff does not increase it.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: result validation reduces downstream reporting on failures and adds only constant per-success metadata.

Scenarios.Scenario: Insert a chat code block into a new untitled editor
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening the untitled editor is the required user-visible operation. The PR now waits for the existing openEditor promise before reporting success, so the command promise tracks the operation rather than adding a new operation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create and open one untitled editor populated with the code block.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one openEditor call per gesture, unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same openEditor call was started without awaiting it; telemetry was emitted immediately.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before the scenario is visibly complete. The diff awaits the same promise and performs reporting only after success.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Notify the owning extension after a successful new-file open.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one notification per successful gesture; canceled opens now emit none.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Enqueued immediately after starting openEditor, including when opening later failed or was canceled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Enqueued after editor opening and not awaited across IPC.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Queue successful insertion telemetry with correlation identifiers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one event per successful open, reduced from one per attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Queued immediately per attempt without the new identifiers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Small synchronous preparation after the required open; delivery is asynchronous.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One editor and one code-block string per explicit gesture; no collection or history scaling.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One open operation per invocation. Reporting is serialized after it, with no concurrency burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Untitled editor creation is intentionally per gesture; no cache is involved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the changed action body and editor-service call count.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Editor activation cost varies with installed language features, but the diff neither duplicates that work nor adds another editor open.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: awaiting the existing critical operation changes completion semantics but adds no expensive work or realistic user-visible delay beyond opening the editor itself.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all six changed files and traced copy, selected-copy, active-editor/notebook insertion, new-file insertion, telemetry, extension-host notification, clipboard IPC, and editor/bulk-edit boundaries. No actionable performance regression was introduced, and the PR does not establish a shipped performance-regression fix requiring blame attribution.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
